body:
_Migrated from issue #1355, filed 2026-08-04._

Found by the v4.1.29 pre-tag refuter gate, on an isolated rig (`cwn-refuter` :8087) with all
eight relevant `cps/` files sha256-verified against `origin/main` first.

**Pre-existing, not a regression** — `update_book_read_status` is unchanged in v4.1.29 apart
from the threshold extraction. But #1340 added the "don't un-finish a book you marked Read"
guard to the *web reader only*, so the majority install still loses the mark to the majority
sync client.

## Repro (default install, `config_read_column = 0`, same user, same book)

```
[1] mark READ in browser   POST /ajax/toggleread/6     -> ub.ReadBook = 1 (FINISHED)
[2] KOReader opens it      PUT /kosync/syncs/progress  -> HTTP 200
    {"document":"d09824c5...","percentage":0.05,"device":"KOReader","device_id":"kobo-clara-1"}
                                                       -> ub.ReadBook = 2 (IN_PROGRESS), 5.0%
[3] control: same 5% via the web reader                -> ub.ReadBook stays 1
```

`GET /book/6` then renders the Read checkbox **unchecked**, plus `KOReader Progress: 5%`. The
user's Read mark is gone because they opened the book on their e-reader — the exact symptom
#1340 is named for.

## Root cause

`cps/progress_syncing/protocols/kosync.py:1188` calls
`update_book_read_status(user, book_id, percentage_float)` with no equivalent of the guard at
`cps/services/reading_position.py:176`, and `update_book_read_status` then writes
`book_read.read_status = new_status` unconditionally (`kosync.py:466-471`).

## The asymmetry, which is the part worth fixing

Same push, only `config_read_column` differs:

| install | after KOReader pushes 5% on a book marked Read | checkbox |
|---|---|---|
| custom column | column stays `1`, `ub.ReadBook` → `2` | **checked** |
| default | `ub.ReadBook` → `2` (the only carrier) | **unchecked** |

`_mark_custom_read_column` is deliberately sticky (`kosync.py:513-517`: *"re-opening a finished
book in KOReader can't silently un-read it"*). So the custom-column carrier already has exactly
the protection the default carrier lacks, and #1344's mirror leaves custom-column installs
**strictly safer than default ones**. The stickiness rationale applies verbatim to `ub.ReadBook`.

## Fix direction

Apply the same downgrade guard on the kosync writer that `reading_position.py:176` applies on
the web-reader writer — a sync must not silently un-read a book — keeping the deliberate escape
hatch that an explicit "mark unread" still clears everything.
title: KOReader sync can un-finish a book marked Read on a default install (the #1340 guard is web-reader-only)
